title: Phishing & Social Engineering Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Protect yourself from phishing scams and social engineering attacks with this comprehensive privacy checklist. Learn to spot threats and secure your data.
intro: Phishing and social engineering attacks target human psychology rather than technical vulnerabilities. This checklist helps you build strong defenses against scammers who try to trick you into revealing personal information or clicking malicious links.

items.task: Always verify sender identity before clicking links or attachments
items.why: Phishing emails often impersonate trusted organizations to steal credentials or install malware on your device.
items.howTo: Check sender email addresses carefully for typos or suspicious domains. When in doubt, contact the organization directly through official channels before responding.

items.task: Enable spam and phishing filters in your email client
items.why: Email filters automatically block most known phishing attempts and suspicious messages before they reach your inbox.
items.howTo: Turn on spam protection in Gmail, Outlook, or your email provider. Consider using additional email security services for enhanced protection.

items.task: Never click links in unexpected or suspicious emails
items.why: Malicious links can redirect you to fake websites designed to steal your login credentials or download malware.
items.howTo: Instead of clicking links, manually type the website URL into your browser or use bookmarks. Hover over links to preview the destination URL first.

items.task: Use a privacy-focused email provider with built-in security features
items.why: Secure email providers offer better protection against phishing attempts and don't scan your emails for advertising purposes.
items.howTo: Consider switching to ProtonMail, Tutanota, or similar encrypted email services that prioritize user privacy and security.

items.task: Use a privacy-focused browser with anti-phishing protection
items.why: Secure browsers like Incognito Browser block malicious websites and protect against tracking that could be used in targeted attacks.
items.howTo: Download Incognito Browser or configure Firefox/Chrome with strict privacy settings. Enable phishing and malware protection in browser settings.

items.task: Always verify website SSL certificates and URLs before entering sensitive information
items.why: Fake websites often use similar URLs or lack proper security certificates to trick users into entering personal data.
items.howTo: Look for the padlock icon in your browser address bar. Check that URLs match exactly (watch for character substitutions). Never enter passwords on HTTP sites.

items.task: Access important websites through bookmarks rather than search results or links
items.why: Attackers can create fake websites that appear in search results or send malicious links that look legitimate.
items.howTo: Bookmark your bank, email, and other important sites. Always use these bookmarks to access accounts rather than clicking links from emails or messages.

items.task: Keep browser security warnings enabled and never ignore them
items.why: Browser warnings alert you to potentially dangerous websites and downloads that could compromise your privacy.
items.howTo: Never disable security warnings in your browser settings. If you see a security warning, do not proceed to the website or download.

items.task: Minimize personal information shared on social media and public profiles
items.why: Scammers use publicly available information to make their attacks more convincing and personalized (spear phishing).
items.howTo: Review privacy settings on Facebook, LinkedIn, and other platforms. Remove or restrict access to personal details like phone numbers, addresses, and family information.

items.task: Always verify unexpected requests for sensitive information through independent channels
items.why: Social engineers often create urgency or impersonate authority figures to pressure victims into sharing confidential data.
items.howTo: If someone calls or emails requesting passwords, account details, or payments, hang up and call the organization directly using official contact information.

items.task: Maintain healthy skepticism about unsolicited offers, urgent requests, and 'too good to be true' opportunities
items.why: Social engineering attacks exploit human emotions like fear, greed, and helpfulness to bypass logical thinking.
items.howTo: Take time to think before responding to urgent requests. Research offers independently. When in doubt, consult with trusted friends or family members.

items.task: Educate family members and colleagues about common social engineering tactics
items.why: Attackers may target your contacts to gain access to your information or use them as stepping stones for larger attacks.
items.howTo: Share information about common scams with family and coworkers. Establish verification procedures for sensitive requests within your household or organization.

items.task: Enable two-factor authentication on all important accounts
items.why: 2FA provides an additional layer of security even if your password is compromised through phishing attacks.
items.howTo: Use authenticator apps like Google Authenticator or Authy instead of SMS when possible. Enable 2FA on email, banking, social media, and work accounts.

items.task: Use unique, strong passwords for every account with a password manager
items.why: If one account is compromised through phishing, unique passwords prevent attackers from accessing your other accounts.
items.howTo: Install a reputable password manager like Bitwarden or 1Password. Generate unique passwords for each account and never reuse passwords across sites.

items.task: Regularly monitor account activity and enable security notifications
items.why: Early detection of unauthorized access can help minimize damage from successful phishing attacks.
items.howTo: Check bank and email account activity weekly. Enable login notifications and security alerts. Report suspicious activity immediately to the service provider.

items.task: Secure account recovery options and backup authentication methods
items.why: Attackers often target recovery emails and phone numbers to gain access to your accounts even with strong passwords.
items.howTo: Use a separate, secure email for account recovery. Keep backup authentication codes in a safe place. Avoid using easily guessed security questions.
